runtime_posture.control_transport: fixed-argv Docker CLI exec/copy through the local Docker daemon; the service has no host TCP or Unix-socket publication

runtime_posture.outbound_probe: docker exec first requires curl --version to exit 0, then invokes curl --noproxy '*' --silent --show-error --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 3 http://198.51.100.1:80/ inside the empty network-none container; probe must exit 7 or 28 with stdout exactly 000 before fixture bytes are read
runtime_posture.cleanup: remove the run-labeled container with docker rm -fv, then prove no run-labeled container, volume, or network remains

required_observations: selected platform manifest and actual Docker image ID match this attestation
all four tmpfs targets and read-only root are present
no anonymous or host data volume is mounted
NetworkMode is none and the container has no additional network attachment
no TCP or Unix-socket port is published to the host
curl --version exits 0, then the fixed numeric outbound probe exits 7 or 28 with stdout exactly 000
the overridden service process binds only to 127.0.0.1:8000 inside the container
disabled integration flags and absent proxy variables match this attestation
GET /health reports both in-memory index sizes=0

limitations: This is static source and OCI metadata evidence, not a container runtime receipt.
The fixed image has no VISION_INDEX_CLEAN_START switch; freshness depends on the attested tmpfs and zero-count preflight.
The service has no drawing-list endpoint; exact post-index identities are bound by the receipt set plus authoritative count three.
The fixed service has no authentication on index or rebuild routes; network-none plus no host publication makes the local Docker daemon the administrative capability boundary for this isolated run.

Index-add creates an in-memory LocalEventBus even with EVENT_BUS_ENABLED=false; EVENT_BUS_USE_LOCAL=true and runtime inspection prevent a Redis path, and explicit rebuild remains required because no index handlers are registered.
The image reports three inconsistent version strings, so only the image digest and source revision identify the substrate.
No image pull, container start, fixture processing, model-quality evaluation, customer-data use, merge, deployment, decision enablement, or pilot is authorized by this attestation.
